text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to project management, especially in software development. Instead of working on a project for many months, teams break the work into smaller parts called sprints. Each sprint lasts about two weeks, and at the end, they have a working piece of the product. Every day, the team has a short meeting called a standup, where everyone shares what they did yesterday, what they will do today, and any problems they have. The team also keeps a backlog, which is a list of all the tasks and features needed. These tasks are often written as user stories, which describe things from the user's perspective. This iterative development process allows for regular feedback and changes, ensuring the final product truly meets customer needs.
